payload.feature:
Close issue #219: a provider's limit refusal arrives after `accepted`, so a gate chain cannot fall to its next judge.

Read the issue, decision 0016 (the judge chain), decision 0041 ruling 3 (a gate whose judges are unavailable parks rather than descends), and the limits section of `docs/guides/agent-library.md`, which already names the fix.

**The defect, measured three times.** The claude driver answers `accepted` the moment the CLI spawns. The account's limit refusal (`rate_limit`, "You've reached your ... limit") arrives after that, and decision 0016 deliberately excludes a mid-session failure from fallback — so an exhausted limit stops every seat that opens on that vendor while the next judge in the chain sits idle. On run `decision-0046-enactment-slice-i--165601b4` the engine smith chained `fable@high -> opus@high` exited 1 twice with empty stderr (seq 3646/3652), both seat transcripts carrying `rate_limit`, and a probe seconds later answered `ok` on both `claude-fable-5-1` and `claude-opus-5`: the limit is per model, opus was serving throughout, and the chain's own second link would have taken the work. The same run parked this way once before in design (seq 2133). Two of that run's six parks are this bug.

**Build it so:**

1. **A provider's pre-session refusal is a determinate start failure.** No turn started, and a limit or auth error in the first records: the driver classifies it as a refusal to start, not as an accepted attempt that failed. The engine's chain then advances to the next judge exactly as it does for a model the machine cannot reach at all. A refusal that arrives after the first turn stays what decision 0016 says it is — this narrows nothing about mid-session failure.
2. **The classification is the driver's, per built-in adapter.** Claude first, because that is where it is measured; state in the code and in the guide what each other built-in adapter does with the same shape, and cover the ones whose wire protocol makes the same distinction available.
3. **The record keeps the refused attempt with its reason**, so the journal shows the chain descending and why, and neither the fold nor any readout invents a success.
4. **A test per built-in driver with a shim that refuses before the first turn**, alongside the existing conformance suite, proving the attempt is classified determinate and the chain advances.
5. **If enacting this needs a ruling** — because it reads on decision 0016's exclusion — write it as a numbered decision with status `proposed` and the context that forced the question, and index it. Never accept a decision; that is the operator's, in the file.

Constraints, binding: do not edit `contracts/*.v1..v8`, `realms.v1..v3`, `seat-record.v1..v3`, `policy/phase-machine.json`, `reference/`, or `fixtures/evaluator/corpus.ndjson`. Re-pin any witness or compose digest that moves. Any test driving a boxed step end to end skips under `BROKKR_HANDS_BOX`. Coverage is exact and literal.

Green before you finish: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, and both `brokkr compile --bundle bundles/self` and `--bundle bundles/verify`. Do not push and do not open a pull request; the operator lands it. Say what you could not verify and what evidence you relied on.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including all three operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Five platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew, Scoop and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```

result.notes: 8 path(s) since b8078c6; outside the docs class: crates/brokkr-cli/tests/driver_conformance.rs crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/tests.rs crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/agent_tests.rs

cargo test --workspace: 64 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

Reviewed 168ec7e (the run's only commit) against the framing for #219. The delivery meets items 1-5: the classifier is per built-in adapter and reads machine-readable fields only, dsh/exec state in code and guide why they cannot, decision 0053 is written `proposed` and indexed, the refused attempt keeps its reason, and there is a refusal shim per built-in in driver_conformance.rs plus classifier/run_seat/engine tests. No frozen contract, policy table, reference or corpus byte was touched; no witness or compose digest moved. Gates I ran here: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean; `compile --bundle bundles/self` and `--bundle bundles/verify` both compile. `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` is green except `brokkr-runtime --test landing_shape::the_classify_gate_reads_the_repositorys_own_docs_class`, which fails on `gpg: signing failed: Inappropriate ioctl for device` — its `git` helper (crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/landing_shape.rs:159) does not disable `commit.gpgsign`, so it inherits the operator's global signing config. That test came in with 900bc85 (decision 0051) and is untouched by this delivery; environmental, not this run's. UNVERIFIED: the exact-coverage gate (scripts/coverage-exact.sh) — it cannot run from this seat and would hit the same gpg failure; and remote CI.

Three findings remain, none fixed by me (read-only seat).

1. MEDIUM — correctness. adapters.rs:2621. Withholding `accepted` until the first work-beginning checkpoint also reclassifies an attempt that is KILLED before its first model turn. process.rs `eof_outcome` returns `Failed` (not `Indeterminate`) when the deadline watchdog fired, and the watchdog SIGKILLs the process tree, so the adapter sends nothing: `Failed` + `accepted: false` + no checkpoints = the engine's structural `failed_to_start`, and the chain descends. Before this commit `accepted` was the first statement of `run_seat`, so that shape was reachable only when the driver could not be spawned at all. Concretely: a vendor outage that hangs the CLI for the whole `seat.limits.timeout_seconds` now walks the chain down every link on the same hanging vendor (each one hanging for a full deadline) before parking, and journals per-model `start_failure_sites` for what was one vendor-wide outage. This contradicts decision 0053 ruling 2's own claim that the change "widens nothing about mid-session failure", and the new agent-library.md:121 line — "a driver that vanishes before any machine-readable refusal is still `indeterminate`" — is false for a timeout. No test covers a deadline kill under the new withholding. This is the operator's ruling to make (either scope the withholding so a timeout keeps its old side of the boundary, or record the widening in 0053 and pin it with a test), which is why it is left standing rather than patched.

2. LOW — security (unbounded harness-controlled data into a durable record). adapters.rs:507. `refusal_reason`'s own doc says the reason is "a single line, clamped, and never empty", but only the `text` excerpt is whitespace-normalised and clamped to 160 chars; `token` is interpolated verbatim. `token` is `event["error"]` from the harness's stream (claude_refusal's `assistant` and `result` arms) — arbitrary-length, newline-bearing, harness-controlled JSON. An agent CLI (or anything standing in for one, which this suite already models with LANETALLY_ADVERSARIAL_SHIM/NOTES_LEAK_SHIM) emitting `{"type":"result","is_error":true,"error":"<200KB with newlines>"}` before the first turn puts the whole blob in the attempt's journaled `error` and in every readout that renders it, breaking the invariant the test name `a_refusal_reason_is_one_bounded_line` asserts. Every other wire-derived field in this file is clamped (<=80-char tool names and targets, the 4000-byte stderr tail). No control decision reads the string — `failed_to_start` stays structural — so this is data hygiene, not a fail-open; hence low, but it is a security-dimension residual and is reported as one rather than folded into correctness.

3. LOW — observability/evidence. adapters.rs:1511 and the buffering in run_seat. Two undocumented consequences: (a) the `transcript` locator row is now buffered until the first turn, though its own comment at the fold says it is journaled early precisely so drilldowns can locate and live-stream a WORKING seat's prose "from the first message" — during a long first turn the live readout can no longer locate the seat; (b) on a refusal the locator is dropped entirely (the conformance test asserts no checkpoint), so a refused attempt has no transcript pointer in the journal — and the seat transcripts carrying `rate_limit` are exactly the evidence #219 was diagnosed from. (b) is forced by the `checkpoints.is_empty()` predicate and is defensible; neither is recorded in decision 0053's Consequences. Related, same anchor: once `refusal` latches, `invoke_stream_json`/`invoke_codex` stop folding the rest of the stream, so in the one shape where a refusal latches while `began_work` is already true (codex `item.*` before `turn.started` — the shape the delivery's own test `a_refusal_after_work_began_is_not_a_failure_to_start` constructs) the attempt proceeds normally but with truncated session_meta: no served model, no usage, no cost, and no thread id for decision 0030 resume.

Returned implement on fire/219-limit-fallback: answered all three residual findings the review left on 168ec7e, committed as 25f2101 (signed, tree clean, not pushed).

MEDIUM (correctness, adapters.rs:2621) — the withheld `accepted` had also moved an attempt the engine's own deadline watchdog kills: the driver is SIGKILLed and reports nothing, `eof_outcome` returns Failed, so a first turn that merely hangs reached the engine as Failed + !accepted + no checkpoint, i.e. the structural fail-to-start shape. One hanging vendor would have walked the chain down every link, each hanging a full deadline, journaling per-model start failures for a vendor-wide stall. Scoped it rather than recording the widening: `AttemptReport` carries `deadline_killed` (set in `DriverProcess::finish` from the watchdog's own flag) and `failed_to_start` reads it as a fourth structural term. We ended that attempt; no provider refused it; decision 0003's ambiguity parks it. Written as decision 0053 ruling 5 with the one shape that changes the other way named explicitly — a driver that hangs its whole deadline BEFORE the handshake used to descend the chain and now parks.

LOW security (adapters.rs:507) — `refusal_reason` interpolated the harness-supplied `token` verbatim while only the excerpt was clamped. Both now go through one `bounded_wire_line`: whitespace collapsed, control characters stripped, clamped to 80 (token, the checkpoint bound for a harness-supplied name) and 160 (excerpt); an empty token falls back to `api_error` so the line never dangles.

LOW observability (adapters.rs:1511) — (a) the buffering of the transcript locator is now stated where the fold records it, in decision 0053's Consequences and in both guides; it is forced by the fail-to-start predicate and is kept. (b) a refused attempt emits no checkpoint, so it now carries `[transcript <kind>/<locator>]` in its reason — the pointer at the evidence #219 was itself diagnosed from. (c) the fold no longer stops at a classified refusal. That was worse than reported: a harness that erred and then WORKED had its remaining stream dropped, so with no checkpoint emitted a completed, billed session was reported as a failure to start and its result discarded. Both folds now read the whole stream; `run_seat` settles the question from whether work began.

Also fixed the pre-existing landing_shape fixture failure the review called environmental: its `git` helper inherited the operator's global `commit.gpgsign` and failed `git commit` on a pinentry it cannot open. One `-c commit.gpgsign=false` on the fixture's own repository; no production code involved. Flagging it because it is outside the three findings.

Gates run here, all green: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` (zero failures, landing_shape included); `compile --bundle bundles/self` and `--bundle bundles/verify`. No frozen contract, `policy/phase-machine.json`, `reference/`, `fixtures/` byte touched; no witness or compose digest moved (nothing pins one over these files, and the digest tests pass).

UNVERIFIED: the exact-coverage gate — `rustup`/`cargo-llvm-cov`/`jq` probes are refused from this seat, so `scripts/coverage-exact.sh` could not be run; every new function and branch (`bounded_wire_line` including its control-character arm, `transcript_locator`'s four exits, the `deadline_killed` term, both refusal-and-work paths) has a test, but the literal gate is CI's. Also unverified: remote CI on this head.

cargo test --workspace: 64 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

Reviewed the whole delivery (168ec7e + 25f2101) against b8078c6 and the #219 framing. The three residuals the first review left are genuinely answered, and I re-derived each answer rather than taking the implementer's word: (1) `AttemptReport.deadline_killed` is set in `DriverProcess::finish` from the watchdog's own flag AFTER the disarm and reap, `failed_to_start` reads it as a fourth structural term, and both the deadline-kill test in process/tests.rs and the predicate test in agent_tests.rs pin it — a hung first turn parks instead of walking the chain down every link; (2) token and excerpt both go through `bounded_wire_line` (whitespace collapsed, control chars stripped, 80/160), pinned by `a_refusal_token_is_bounded_like_every_other_wire_field` including an ESC-bearing 400-char blob through the arm that actually reads the harness field; (3) neither fold stops at a classified refusal — `refusal = refusal.or(classified)` keeps the first and reads on — and `a_harness_that_errs_and_then_works_keeps_its_session_and_its_result` proves a codex session that erred then worked keeps its thread id, its usage and its own succeeded result.

Framing items 1-5 all met. Item 1: the refusal is classified only at `assistant_turns == 0` / `turn == 0`, and I checked that `assistant_turns` increments on EVERY assistant record and that every assistant record emits at least one `seat-turn` row, so the fold's counter and `run_seat`'s `began_work` cannot disagree. Item 2: per-adapter, and every one of the four `Invocation` construction sites states its position (claude+lanetally share `invoke_stream_json`, codex classifies, dsh and exec state why they cannot); no classifier reads prose, pinned by the negative cases in `claude_pre_session_refusals_are_read_from_machine_fields_only` and `codex_pre_session_refusals_are_machine_events_not_prose`. Item 3: the engine test proves `start_failure`/`start_failure_sites` and `chain_index` advance, and `start_failure_sites` delegates to the same predicate so the deadline term is consistent for panels too; `AttemptReport` is not `Serialize`, so the new field cannot reach the journal. Item 4: a refusal shim per built-in in driver_conformance.rs, plus the two negative shims for dsh/exec. Item 5: decision 0053 is `proposed`, indexed, and its Alternatives section records the ruling-5 question the withholding forced, including the one shape that changes the other way (a driver hanging its whole deadline before the handshake used to descend and now parks).

Structural checks I ran: no frozen byte touched (diff is 14 files, none under contracts/, policy/, reference/ or fixtures/); no witness or compose digest is pinned over adapter source, and the digest suites pass; `accepted` is read by nothing but `failed_to_start` (grep), so withholding it changes no journal event; `begins_work`'s exclusion list is complete against every `emit` site's `step` value (transcript, harness-started, turn-started, item-started, item-completed, seat-turn, turn-completed, exec-started) and the terminal `*-session-finished` row is sent directly rather than through `emit`, so it always follows `accepted`; the protocol reader imposes no accepted-before-result ordering, so a refusal's `result` with no `accepted` is contract-legal.

Gates run here, all green: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` (64 test-suite summaries, 0 failed, landing_shape included now that its fixture stops inheriting the operator's commit.gpgsign); `compile --bundle bundles/self` and `--bundle bundles/verify` both compile. Log kept at .forge/rev219-tests.txt (gitignored; working tree clean, nothing pushed).

Three findings remain, all LOW, none fixed by me (read-only seat).

1. LOW — security / data hygiene. adapters.rs:2885 (helper at 2654). The transcript locator appended to a refusal reason is the ONE harness-supplied field in that string that does not pass through `bounded_wire_line`. `transcript_locator`'s comment claims "both halves are already clamped where they are recorded", but `Transcript::record` only does `locator.chars().take(80)` — it does not collapse whitespace or strip control characters. A harness emitting `{"type":"system","subtype":"init","session_id":"abc\n\u001b[2Kprovider ok"}` before its refusal puts newlines and ANSI escapes into the attempt's durable `error`, so the composed reason is not the single bounded line `refusal_reason`'s own doc and ruling 6 assert, and a terminal readout of a fail-to-start attempt can be made to render forged lines. Bounded to 80 chars and no control decision reads the string, so it is low — but it is exactly the class the same commit fixed for the token, and it is the one field left out. No test asserts the COMPOSED reason is one line: `a_refused_attempt_names_its_transcript_only_when_there_is_one` only exercises well-formed locators. Reported as a security-dimension residual rather than folded into correctness.

2. LOW — correctness, an unmeasured classification. adapters.rs:585. The `rate_limit_event` arm fires unconditionally: any record of that type before the first turn becomes "provider refused before the first turn: rate_limit", with no read of a status or rejected field. The other two claude shapes are the ones #219 measured; this one is asserted ("the `rate_limit_event` lifecycle message newer CLIs emit") and it is the only one of the three that a harness can plausibly emit as an ADVISORY rather than a rejection. The structural damage is bounded and self-correcting — once any turn checkpoints, `began_work` discards the latched refusal — so the only reachable consequence is a seat that would have failed anyway being journaled as a refusal-to-start with a misattributed reason, and descending instead of parking. Worth the operator's eye because the decision's table states the shape as measured fact.

3. LOW — observability. adapters.rs:2880-2893. A refused attempt now emits no checkpoint AT ALL, which is broader than the consequence decision 0053 records ("a refused attempt has no transcript checkpoint"): before this delivery the same refusal also produced a `<driver>-session-finished` row carrying exit code, served model, effort and usage. Every readout keyed on that row — brokkr-view's attempt panel arm at brokkr-view/src/lib.rs:1250, muninn's usage and cost aggregation — therefore sees nothing for the attempt, and any usage or cost the harness reported in its error `result` is dropped twice over (the fold returns before folding that record's `usage`/`total_cost_usd`, and `run_seat` then discards the record). For a per-model limit or auth refusal that figure is zero, which is why this is low and not higher; it is reported because it is an unrecorded change to journaled shape rather than a bug in the fix.

Not findings, but flagged for the operator: (a) decision 0053 ruling 5 deliberately leaves the OTHER shape of a limit refusal uncovered — a claude CLI that blocks waiting for the limit to reset is a deadline kill, so it parks and the chain does not fall. #219 measured a fast exit-1, so the measured defect is fixed, and 0053 states the scope ("the case fallback exists for is a provider that refuses fast, not one that hangs"); worth knowing that the #219 park class is only partly closed. (b) 168ec7e is unsigned (`%G?` = N) while 25f2101 is signed (G).

UNVERIFIED: the exact-coverage gate — `command -v cargo-llvm-cov` and every probe form the script needs are refused from this seat, so `scripts/coverage-exact.sh` could not run. I read the new code against the new tests instead and found a test for every new function and, as far as I could trace by hand, every new branch (`bounded_wire_line`'s control arm, `refusal_reason`'s empty-token and empty-excerpt exits, all four `claude_refusal` arms with both `unwrap_or("api_error")` fallbacks, both `codex_refusal` field fallbacks, `transcript_locator`'s four exits, `begins_work` both ways, the `deadline_killed` term, and both refusal-and-work paths) — but the literal gate is CI's, not this seat's. Also unverified: remote CI on this head, and the #219 fix against a live exhausted account (the evidence is the shim suite plus the run transcripts quoted in the issue and in decision 0053's Context).
